title: Social media manager security: how to protect brand accounts on your Mac
metaTitle: Social media manager security: protect your brand on Mac
description: Learn how to secure social media accounts, manage credentials, and audit access on your Mac to prevent costly security breaches.
intro: Social media manager security is a critical part of your job because you act as the gatekeeper for your brand identity. A single compromised account can cause significant financial and reputational damage to your organization.
tldr: 52% of companies reported a social media cyberattack last year.
Remediating a hacked corporate account costs $97,000 on average.
Use a dedicated password manager to avoid credential reuse.
Enable hardware-based multi-factor authentication for all brand accounts.
Audit third-party app connections in your social media settings monthly.

blocks.text: The cost of poor security management

When you manage multiple social media accounts, the risk of a breach is constant. The cost is not just about the time you spend fixing the problem. It is about the loss of trust from your audience and potential revenue impact.

The $97,000 figure covers remediation costs. This includes technical recovery, legal consultations, and public relations efforts to manage the fallout. If your brand is regulated, you must follow your company policy regarding data handling and incident reporting immediately.
Why social media accounts get compromised

Most security issues stem from human error rather than technical failures. You are likely juggling personal and professional accounts on the same device. This makes it easy to reuse passwords or click on a phishing link disguised as a platform update.

items: Credential reuse: 94% of users reuse passwords across different platforms.
Always-on culture: The pressure to stay connected makes you more likely to ignore security alerts.
Sophisticated phishing: Impersonation attacks have risen by 50% due to AI tools.
Lack of policy: 75% of businesses operate without a formal social media security policy.

blocks.text: Fixes for social media manager security on Mac
You do not need expensive software to improve your baseline security. Start by hardening your Mac and changing how you store your credentials.

items: Use a dedicated password manager like 1Password or Bitwarden. Never rely on browser-saved passwords.
Enable multi-factor authentication. Use an authenticator app like Authy or a hardware key instead of SMS codes.
Audit third-party apps. Go to the settings of your social platforms and remove any app that no longer needs access.
Update your Mac. Go to System Settings > General > Software Update to ensure your OS is current.
Review permissions. Check System Settings > Privacy & Security to see which apps have access to your camera or microphone.

blocks.text: If you share accounts with a team, use a social media management tool that supports role-based access. This way, you never have to share the actual account password with anyone.
blocks.title: Use role-based access

faq.question: Is it safe to save passwords in Chrome?
faq.answer: It is safer to use a dedicated password manager like 1Password or Bitwarden. These apps provide better encryption and are not tied to your browser's history or potential vulnerabilities.

faq.question: How often should I audit my social media security?
faq.answer: Perform a security audit once a month. Check for new devices, remove old third-party app connections, and rotate passwords for any account that has been accessed by a former team member.

faq.question: What is the best way to do MFA?
faq.answer: Use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy. If your organization allows it, a physical security key is the most secure option available.
